nodes.name: RootSolver
nodes.capability: Resolve any presented problem by locating it within the most general reusable structure of Problem Solving and routing downward through a conceptual decomposition.
nodes.accepts: Any situation, question, goal, discrepancy, or opportunity presented as requiring resolution.
nodes.produces: A bounded resolution synthesized from an abstraction-guided conceptual decomposition.
nodes.boundary: Owns the complete problem space; descendants expose narrower bounded capabilities while this node remains the universal ingress.
nodes.excludes: Domain routines and fixed task sequences treated as universal structure.

nodes.name: Problem Constitution
nodes.capability: Constitutes a resolvable problem by integrating the relevant present condition, valued destination, and governing boundary.
nodes.accepts: An experienced concern, discrepancy, opportunity, or question.
nodes.produces: A bounded problem whose current state, success conditions, and admissible scope are explicit.
nodes.boundary: Defines what is to be resolved without explaining causes or selecting interventions.
nodes.excludes: Causal diagnosis, option design, commitment, execution, and feedback control.

nodes.name: Situation Characterization
nodes.capability: Forms a relevant account of the conditions from which resolution must begin.
nodes.accepts: Observations, claims, context, and unresolved discrepancies.
nodes.produces: A differentiated representation of the pertinent present situation.
nodes.boundary: Characterizes what currently obtains and what remains unknown.
nodes.excludes: Desired outcomes, causal explanations, and intervention proposals.

nodes.name: Outcome Valuation
nodes.capability: Determines what improvement means and how satisfactory resolution can be recognized.
nodes.accepts: Needs, purposes, preferences, obligations, and candidate outcome properties.
nodes.produces: Prioritized success criteria and tolerable residual conditions.
nodes.boundary: Defines valued ends and evaluation standards.
nodes.excludes: Present-state description, causal modeling, and choice among interventions.

nodes.name: Boundary Constitution
nodes.capability: Determines which conditions, interests, resources, and effects belong inside the problem.
nodes.accepts: Context, affected interests, dependencies, constraints, and available agency.
nodes.produces: An explicit scope with relevant inclusions, exclusions, and non-negotiable limits.
nodes.boundary: Sets the resolution envelope within which other capabilities operate.
nodes.excludes: Diagnosing mechanisms or deciding what action to take.

nodes.name: Explanatory Understanding
nodes.capability: Builds a warranted account of why the problem persists and where change can propagate.
nodes.accepts: A constituted problem plus observations, records, hypotheses, and uncertainty.
nodes.produces: An evidence-calibrated model of mechanisms, dependencies, and leverage.
nodes.boundary: Explains the situation sufficiently to inform intervention design.
nodes.excludes: Generating, choosing, or enacting a resolution.

nodes.name: Evidence Appraisal
nodes.capability: Establishes what information deserves reliance and with what confidence.
nodes.accepts: Observations, testimony, measurements, records, and competing claims.
nodes.produces: A weighted evidence base with gaps, conflicts, and confidence made explicit.
nodes.boundary: Assesses informational warrant rather than constructing the full explanation.
nodes.excludes: Value judgments and intervention selection.

nodes.name: Mechanism Modeling
nodes.capability: Represents the relationships through which conditions generate, sustain, or alter outcomes.
nodes.accepts: A bounded situation and appraised evidence.
nodes.produces: A causal or functional model identifying dependencies and potential leverage.
nodes.boundary: Models change-bearing relationships whether physical, social, logical, or informational.
nodes.excludes: Judging desired outcomes or committing to an intervention.

nodes.name: Uncertainty Representation
nodes.capability: Represents material unknowns, variability, ambiguity, and model limitations.
nodes.accepts: Evidence, mechanism models, disputed interpretations, and possible future conditions.
nodes.produces: A calibrated uncertainty structure showing what is unknown and why it matters.
nodes.boundary: Preserves uncertainty for later design and judgment instead of forcing false certainty.
nodes.excludes: Resolving value conflicts or selecting a course of action.

nodes.name: Resolution Synthesis
nodes.capability: Constructs coherent candidate ways to move the constituted situation toward valued outcomes.
nodes.accepts: A constituted problem, explanatory model, uncertainties, and available means.
nodes.produces: Distinct, internally coherent intervention candidates with anticipated effects.
nodes.boundary: Creates and develops possibilities without finally adopting one.
nodes.excludes: Final commitment, authorization, and enactment.

nodes.name: Intervention Generation
nodes.capability: Generates materially distinct mechanisms for changing the problem situation.
nodes.accepts: Leverage points, success criteria, boundary conditions, and available capabilities.
nodes.produces: A varied set of candidate interventions rather than superficial variants.
nodes.boundary: Expands the feasible possibility space.
nodes.excludes: Final comparison, adoption, and implementation.

nodes.name: Consequence Anticipation
nodes.capability: Projects intended, indirect, delayed, and failure consequences of candidate interventions.
nodes.accepts: Candidate interventions, mechanism models, affected interests, and uncertainty.
nodes.produces: Conditional consequence profiles across relevant criteria and contexts.
nodes.boundary: Examines what candidates may produce without deciding which should prevail.
nodes.excludes: Commitment and real-world execution.

nodes.name: Configuration Integration
nodes.capability: Combines compatible intervention elements into resolutions whose parts support rather than undermine one another.
nodes.accepts: Candidate mechanisms, consequence profiles, constraints, and dependencies.
nodes.produces: Coherent candidate configurations with internal conflicts exposed or resolved.
nodes.boundary: Ensures candidate-level systemic fit before selection.
nodes.excludes: Choosing or authorizing a configuration.

nodes.name: Resolution Commitment
nodes.capability: Converts evaluated possibilities into a defensible adopted course under tradeoffs and uncertainty.
nodes.accepts: Coherent candidates, consequence profiles, success criteria, uncertainty, and decision authority.
nodes.produces: An adopted resolution with rationale, accepted risks, and commitment conditions.
nodes.boundary: Determines which course will govern action.
nodes.excludes: Generating the option space or carrying the decision into effect.

nodes.name: Comparative Judgment
nodes.capability: Evaluates candidates across plural success criteria and unavoidable tradeoffs.
nodes.accepts: Candidate configurations, consequence profiles, and prioritized criteria.
nodes.produces: A transparent comparative assessment including dominated and non-comparable alternatives.
nodes.boundary: Structures preference among candidates without itself establishing adoption.
nodes.excludes: Option generation, authorization, and execution.

nodes.name: Robustness Judgment
nodes.capability: Tests whether a candidate remains acceptable across uncertainty, disruption, and plausible error.
nodes.accepts: Candidate resolutions, uncertainty structure, failure modes, and reversibility information.
nodes.produces: Risk exposure, robustness conditions, safeguards, and residual uncertainty.
nodes.boundary: Assesses resilience of choice rather than operational progress.
nodes.excludes: Ongoing feedback control after enactment.

nodes.name: Adoption Formation
nodes.capability: Establishes the authority, ownership, and willingness required for a resolution to govern action.
nodes.accepts: Comparative assessments, risk judgments, affected commitments, and decision rights.
nodes.produces: A selected and owned resolution with explicit conditions for reconsideration.
nodes.boundary: Closes deliberation provisionally and creates actionable commitment.
nodes.excludes: Mobilizing resources or performing the intervention.

nodes.name: Resolution Realization
nodes.capability: Translates an adopted resolution into coordinated changes in the world.
nodes.accepts: An adopted resolution, available agency, resources, and operational conditions.
nodes.produces: Enacted changes corresponding to the resolution's intended mechanism.
nodes.boundary: Makes the resolution real while preserving its governing intent.
nodes.excludes: Defining success, explaining the original problem, or reassessing outcomes.

nodes.name: Operational Translation
nodes.capability: Converts conceptual commitment into executable responsibilities, dependencies, and action conditions.
nodes.accepts: An adopted resolution and the operating context in which it must occur.
nodes.produces: An actionable configuration linking intent to concrete agency.
nodes.boundary: Specifies how the chosen mechanism becomes operable.
nodes.excludes: Selecting the resolution or evaluating its eventual effects.

nodes.name: Capability Mobilization
nodes.capability: Brings required agency, resources, access, and coordination into effective alignment.
nodes.accepts: Operational requirements, available capabilities, dependencies, and constraints.
nodes.produces: A functioning arrangement capable of performing the intervention.
nodes.boundary: Assembles and coordinates the means of realization.
nodes.excludes: Outcome valuation and post-action learning.

nodes.name: Intervention Performance
nodes.capability: Carries the selected mechanism through its relevant interactions with the problem situation.
nodes.accepts: An operational configuration, mobilized capabilities, and real conditions.
nodes.produces: Concrete state changes and observable effects.
nodes.boundary: Performs the intervention rather than merely planning or resourcing it.
nodes.excludes: Interpreting whether observed effects constitute success.

nodes.name: Resolution Regulation
nodes.capability: Keeps problem solving responsive by comparing unfolding reality with intent and revising the resolution system when warranted.
nodes.accepts: Success criteria, enacted changes, observations, deviations, and emerging conditions.
nodes.produces: Corrections, learning, escalation, or closure grounded in feedback.
nodes.boundary: Regulates the whole resolution across time without assuming the initial framing remains correct.
nodes.excludes: Treating execution completion alone as proof of resolution.

nodes.name: Outcome Sensing
nodes.capability: Detects relevant changes, side effects, and signals produced during and after intervention.
nodes.accepts: Observable conditions, success indicators, stakeholder experience, and anomaly signals.
nodes.produces: Timely evidence about outcomes and emerging conditions.
nodes.boundary: Acquires resolution-relevant feedback.
nodes.excludes: Explaining discrepancies or deciding revisions.

nodes.name: Discrepancy Interpretation
nodes.capability: Determines what differences between intended and observed outcomes imply about performance, models, criteria, or framing.
nodes.accepts: Outcome evidence, expectations, uncertainty, and success criteria.
nodes.produces: A localized account of why resolution is succeeding, failing, or becoming obsolete.
nodes.boundary: Diagnoses feedback at the level where revision is needed.
nodes.excludes: Executing the resulting revision.

nodes.name: Adaptive Revision
nodes.capability: Revises framing, understanding, design, commitment, or realization in response to interpreted feedback.
nodes.accepts: Diagnosed discrepancies, emerging opportunities, changed constraints, and retained learning.
nodes.produces: A corrected resolution state or a justified closure decision.
nodes.boundary: Routes learning back to the appropriate problem-solving dimension.
nodes.excludes: Assuming every discrepancy requires the same kind of correction.

nodes.name: System Shaping
nodes.capability: Intentionally configure or transform interacting structures so their combined behavior produces valued conditions over time.
nodes.accepts: A system whose structures, relationships, incentives, or capacities require deliberate change.
nodes.produces: A coherent system configuration aligned with desired behavior and viable operation.
nodes.boundary: Governs resolution through structural intervention in an interacting whole.
nodes.excludes: Explanation without change, isolated object repair, and expression whose value is primarily interpretive.

nodes.name: Institutional Arrangement Design
nodes.capability: Design durable rules, roles, incentives, and authorities that coordinate collective behavior.
nodes.accepts: Collective purposes, affected interests, behavioral mechanisms, authority, and enforcement constraints.
nodes.produces: A legitimate and operable institutional arrangement.
nodes.boundary: Shapes rule-governed collective interaction rather than a single transaction or physical artifact.
nodes.excludes: Purely technical architectures and informal advice without institutional force.

nodes.name: Tax System Design
nodes.capability: Configure compulsory public revenue collection so fiscal, distributive, behavioral, and administrative requirements remain jointly viable.
nodes.accepts: Revenue needs, economic structure, distributional aims, administrative capacity, and legitimacy constraints.
nodes.produces: An implementable tax architecture with rates, bases, collection rules, and safeguards.
nodes.boundary: Designs the tax system as an integrated institution.
nodes.excludes: Drafting one tax form or forecasting revenue under a fixed tax code.

nodes.name: Revenue Sufficiency
nodes.capability: Align a revenue system's yield, stability, and growth with public financing requirements.
nodes.accepts: Expenditure needs, candidate bases, rates, compliance assumptions, and economic scenarios.
nodes.produces: A resilient revenue envelope and financing mix.
nodes.boundary: Owns fiscal yield and stability.
nodes.excludes: Distributional legitimacy and collection operations.

nodes.name: Distributional Incidence
nodes.capability: Shape how institutional burdens and benefits fall across materially different groups.
nodes.accepts: Household and firm characteristics, candidate rules, behavioral responses, and equity principles.
nodes.produces: A distribution profile aligned with explicit fairness commitments.
nodes.boundary: Owns effective incidence rather than statutory labels.
nodes.excludes: Aggregate revenue sufficiency and administrative execution.

nodes.name: Administrative Operability
nodes.capability: Fit institutional rules to the state's ability to identify, assess, collect, enforce, and adjudicate.
nodes.accepts: Proposed rules, data availability, workforce, technology, informality, and enforcement capacity.
nodes.produces: Rules and processes that can be administered with tolerable cost and leakage.
nodes.boundary: Owns institutional executability.
nodes.excludes: Choosing distributive values or macroeconomic objectives.

nodes.name: Behavioral Alignment
nodes.capability: Align incentives and compliance conditions with desired participation while limiting harmful avoidance and distortion.
nodes.accepts: Candidate rules, actor responses, enforcement credibility, and valued activities.
nodes.produces: An incentive structure with anticipated adaptation and countermeasures.
nodes.boundary: Owns behavior induced by the arrangement.
nodes.excludes: Revenue accounting and moral judgment about burden sharing.

nodes.name: Service System Shaping
nodes.capability: Shape interactions, handoffs, capacity, and feedback through which a service produces outcomes for recipients.
nodes.accepts: A recurring service journey with multiple actors, touchpoints, constraints, and outcome failures.
nodes.produces: A coordinated service system capable of reliable recipient outcomes.
nodes.boundary: Owns the whole service-producing arrangement across encounters.
nodes.excludes: A single professional act or a product operating without a service journey.

nodes.name: Care Outcome Improvement
nodes.capability: Improve health outcomes by reshaping the clinical and supportive care system around a defined population.
nodes.accepts: A population, preventable adverse outcomes, care mechanisms, and delivery constraints.
nodes.produces: An evidence-calibrated care configuration reducing avoidable harm.
nodes.boundary: Targets population outcomes through care-system change.
nodes.excludes: Treatment selection for one isolated encounter.

nodes.name: Heart-Failure Readmission Reduction
nodes.capability: Reduce avoidable post-discharge hospital returns among heart-failure patients while preserving safety and access.
nodes.accepts: Heart-failure admissions, discharge conditions, patient risks, community capacity, and readmission evidence.
nodes.produces: A risk-sensitive transition and follow-up system with measurable readmission reduction.
nodes.boundary: Owns the transition from inpatient stabilization through early community recovery.
nodes.excludes: Preventing clinically necessary readmission by withholding care.

nodes.name: Clinical Stability
nodes.capability: Establish and preserve sufficient physiological stability for safe transition between care settings.
nodes.accepts: Clinical status, treatment response, comorbidities, and deterioration risks.
nodes.produces: Explicit stability conditions and escalation triggers.
nodes.boundary: Owns clinical readiness and deterioration risk.
nodes.excludes: Patient learning and cross-provider coordination.

nodes.name: Self-Care Capability
nodes.capability: Enable recipients and caregivers to perform the understanding, monitoring, and action required between service encounters.
nodes.accepts: Required behaviors, literacy, resources, preferences, and caregiver availability.
nodes.produces: Demonstrated capability with barriers and supports addressed.
nodes.boundary: Owns recipient agency outside formal encounters.
nodes.excludes: Clinical stabilization and provider capacity.

nodes.name: Continuity Coordination
nodes.capability: Preserve responsibility, information, and treatment coherence across organizational and temporal handoffs.
nodes.accepts: Care plan, actors, records, dependencies, and handoff risks.
nodes.produces: Named ownership and reliable cross-setting continuity.
nodes.boundary: Owns linkage across care boundaries.
nodes.excludes: The content of clinical treatment itself.

nodes.name: Early Risk Detection
nodes.capability: Detect worsening conditions early enough for a lower-intensity corrective response.
nodes.accepts: Risk markers, patient reports, measurements, and response capacity.
nodes.produces: Timely alerts linked to proportionate escalation.
nodes.boundary: Owns surveillance-to-response latency.
nodes.excludes: Long-term outcome evaluation without immediate action.

nodes.name: Software System Shaping
nodes.capability: Shape computational responsibilities, interfaces, state, and operational qualities into a coherent software system.
nodes.accepts: Required behaviors, existing or proposed software structures, workloads, and operational constraints.
nodes.produces: A software architecture whose component interactions sustain required qualities.
nodes.boundary: Owns software-wide structural coherence and operational behavior.
nodes.excludes: Implementing an isolated function without architectural consequences.

nodes.name: Continuity-Preserving System Evolution
nodes.capability: Transform a functioning system incrementally while preserving critical service and maintaining recovery paths.
nodes.accepts: A live system, target structural change, continuity obligations, dependencies, and operational evidence.
nodes.produces: A staged transformation with bounded exposure and reversible transitions.
nodes.boundary: Owns structural change under uninterrupted-operation constraints.
nodes.excludes: Greenfield design and transformations that permit a full shutdown.

nodes.name: Monolith-to-Microservices Migration
nodes.capability: Redistribute a monolith's capabilities, state, and operations into independently evolvable services without user-visible downtime.
nodes.accepts: A live monolith, domain behavior, dependency structure, reliability objectives, and delivery capacity.
nodes.produces: A staged service architecture with preserved behavior and controlled cutover.
nodes.boundary: Owns the architectural transition rather than advocating microservices in principle.
nodes.excludes: A big-bang rewrite or arbitrary codebase partitioning.

nodes.name: Responsibility Boundaries
nodes.capability: Partition system behavior into cohesive ownership units with explicit contracts.
nodes.accepts: Business capabilities, change coupling, data dependencies, and team ownership.
nodes.produces: Bounded responsibilities and stable interaction contracts.
nodes.boundary: Owns semantic and ownership separation.
nodes.excludes: Traffic cutover and runtime observability.

nodes.name: State Continuity
nodes.capability: Preserve correctness and authority of changing state while ownership moves across system boundaries.
nodes.accepts: Data models, invariants, writes, reads, migration stages, and failure modes.
nodes.produces: Explicit state ownership, synchronization, reconciliation, and cutover rules.
nodes.boundary: Owns state correctness during transition.
nodes.excludes: Service responsibility selection.

nodes.name: Traffic Transition
nodes.capability: Shift live interactions between old and new realizations without violating availability or behavior.
nodes.accepts: Compatible implementations, routing controls, capacity evidence, and rollback conditions.
nodes.produces: A progressive, observable, and reversible cutover.
nodes.boundary: Owns live request or event routing during replacement.
nodes.excludes: Defining component semantics and long-term data ownership.

nodes.name: Operational Observability
nodes.capability: Make system behavior, degradation, dependencies, and change effects detectable at actionable resolution.
nodes.accepts: Runtime interactions, service objectives, telemetry, and failure hypotheses.
nodes.produces: Correlated signals and decision thresholds for safe operation.
nodes.boundary: Owns operational visibility.
nodes.excludes: Performing remediation or defining business boundaries.

nodes.name: Provision Configuration Design
nodes.capability: Configure a bounded set of consumable provisions so safety, adequacy, preference, resources, and repeated use remain jointly viable.
nodes.accepts: Recipient needs, consumable options, hazards, resources, preferences, and a provision horizon.
nodes.produces: A coherent provision configuration across recipients and occasions.
nodes.boundary: Owns selection and arrangement of consumable offerings.
nodes.excludes: Agricultural production and isolated preparation technique.

nodes.name: Household Meal-Plan Design
nodes.capability: Configure meals across a household and time horizon so members can eat safely, adequately, acceptably, and practically.
nodes.accepts: Household members, allergy constraints, nutrition needs, preferences, schedule, budget, and kitchen capacity.
nodes.produces: A feasible meal schedule with shared components and safe adaptations.
nodes.boundary: Owns the multi-day household meal configuration.
nodes.excludes: Clinical allergy diagnosis and preparation of one dish.

nodes.name: Safety Compatibility
nodes.capability: Ensure every offered provision and its handling remain compatible with recipient-specific hazards and exclusions.
nodes.accepts: Recipient hazard profiles, ingredients, substitutions, handling paths, and contamination risks.
nodes.produces: A recipient-by-offering safety map with controlled preparation rules.
nodes.boundary: Owns hazard exclusion and cross-contact control.
nodes.excludes: Nutritional adequacy and taste preference.

nodes.name: Nutritional Coverage
nodes.capability: Compose provisions whose combined nutrient and energy profile adequately covers recipients over the relevant horizon.
nodes.accepts: Recipient requirements, portions, ingredients, and temporal consumption pattern.
nodes.produces: An adequate nutritional profile with material gaps exposed.
nodes.boundary: Owns aggregate nourishment across time.
nodes.excludes: Allergen safety and culinary identity.

nodes.name: Recipient Acceptance
nodes.capability: Fit provisions to preferences, familiarity, autonomy, and sensory tolerance sufficiently for actual uptake.
nodes.accepts: Recipient preferences, aversions, cultural expectations, and candidate offerings.
nodes.produces: An offering set likely to be willingly consumed.
nodes.boundary: Owns practical acceptability.
nodes.excludes: Hazard safety and resource efficiency.

nodes.name: Preparation Flow
nodes.capability: Arrange preparation, storage, reuse, and serving so a provision configuration is feasible with available time and facilities.
nodes.accepts: Menu components, kitchen capacity, schedule, storage, and handling constraints.
nodes.produces: A workable production and serving pattern.
nodes.boundary: Owns household operational flow.
nodes.excludes: Nutritional valuation and preference formation.

nodes.name: Organizational Capability Transformation
nodes.capability: Transform an organization’s interacting capabilities, resources, governance, and learning so it can reliably produce a materially higher level of performance.
nodes.accepts: An organization, performance gap, capability base, resource horizon, and operating constraints.
nodes.produces: A staged, self-reinforcing organizational capability system.
nodes.boundary: Owns durable performance capacity rather than a one-off result.
nodes.excludes: Selecting a single tactic or replacing personnel without systemic change.

nodes.name: Competitive Club Rebuilding
nodes.capability: Rebuild a sports club's sporting and organizational system toward durable competitive standing.
nodes.accepts: Current squad, sporting identity, staff, finances, facilities, league context, and time horizon.
nodes.produces: A staged club model capable of sustained target performance.
nodes.boundary: Owns the club-wide competitive system.
nodes.excludes: Planning one match or purchasing players without organizational integration.

nodes.name: Sporting Model Coherence
nodes.capability: Align playing identity, coaching, recruitment, and performance support around compatible competitive demands.
nodes.accepts: Competitive context, desired identity, squad traits, coaching methods, and performance evidence.
nodes.produces: A coherent sporting model guiding decisions across seasons.
nodes.boundary: Owns how the club intends to compete.
nodes.excludes: Financial solvency and governance authority.

nodes.name: Talent Portfolio Evolution
nodes.capability: Evolve the distribution of capability, age, potential, availability, and value across a talent population.
nodes.accepts: Current talent, performance demands, development curves, contracts, and acquisition options.
nodes.produces: A balanced talent portfolio with succession and optionality.
nodes.boundary: Owns portfolio-level talent composition over time.
nodes.excludes: Daily coaching and financial control outside talent decisions.

nodes.name: Performance Infrastructure
nodes.capability: Provide the analytical, medical, physical, technical, and facility support through which talent becomes available performance.
nodes.accepts: Sporting demands, staff capabilities, health evidence, data, and facilities.
nodes.produces: An integrated support system improving readiness and development.
nodes.boundary: Owns enabling infrastructure around performers.
nodes.excludes: Squad selection and governance.

nodes.name: Financial Resilience
nodes.capability: Maintain an organization's capacity to pursue its purpose through shocks, timing mismatches, and uncertain returns.
nodes.accepts: Revenues, costs, assets, obligations, scenarios, and strategic priorities.
nodes.produces: A sustainable resource envelope with risk limits and contingency capacity.
nodes.boundary: Owns solvency, flexibility, and resource endurance.
nodes.excludes: Defining the sporting model.

nodes.name: Governance Continuity
nodes.capability: Preserve strategic direction, accountable authority, and decision quality across personnel changes and performance volatility.
nodes.accepts: Decision rights, strategy, leadership roles, incentives, and review mechanisms.
nodes.produces: Stable strategic stewardship with explicit accountability.
nodes.boundary: Owns organizational direction and authority continuity.
nodes.excludes: Executing specialist sporting work.

nodes.name: SaaS Pricing Design
nodes.capability: Configure a software service's price metric, packaging, levels, and commercial conditions to align customer value with adoption and sustainable economics.
nodes.accepts: Customer segments, alternatives, value drivers, usage, costs, positioning, and competitive uncertainty.
nodes.produces: A testable pricing architecture and adjustment policy.
nodes.boundary: Owns the integrated price-and-package institution for a SaaS offering.
nodes.excludes: Negotiating one deal or calculating cost-plus markup alone.

nodes.name: Value Correspondence
nodes.capability: Align what is charged with the magnitude and manner of value recipients obtain.
nodes.accepts: Customer outcomes, willingness evidence, value drivers, and candidate charging metrics.
nodes.produces: A value-linked basis for pricing and differentiation.
nodes.boundary: Owns correspondence between benefit and charge.
nodes.excludes: Competitive signaling and unit-cost sufficiency.

nodes.name: Market Position Signaling
nodes.capability: Use an offering's commercial structure to communicate its intended comparative position and quality meaning.
nodes.accepts: Alternatives, target identity, buyer expectations, and candidate offers.
nodes.produces: A legible position relative to substitutes.
nodes.boundary: Owns market interpretation of the offer.
nodes.excludes: Delivery cost and customer qualification.

nodes.name: Customer Self-Selection
nodes.capability: Structure alternatives so recipients sort themselves into suitable levels without excessive friction or exploitation.
nodes.accepts: Segment needs, usage patterns, willingness, complexity tolerance, and package options.
nodes.produces: A comprehensible choice architecture with useful segmentation.
nodes.boundary: Owns customer sorting across offers.
nodes.excludes: Product fulfillment and aggregate financial viability.

nodes.name: Commercial Viability
nodes.capability: Ensure an offering can fund acquisition, delivery, support, development, and risk at its expected scale.
nodes.accepts: Prices, volumes, retention, costs, expansion, and uncertainty.
nodes.produces: Sustainable unit economics and viability thresholds.
nodes.boundary: Owns economic endurance of the offering.
nodes.excludes: Determining customer value or brand meaning.

nodes.name: Care Allocation Design
nodes.capability: Design rules that allocate limited care capacity across competing needs according to clinical consequence, equity, and operational feasibility.
nodes.accepts: Patient needs, urgency evidence, scarce capabilities, timing, and ethical constraints.
nodes.produces: A defensible allocation protocol with escalation and reassessment.
nodes.boundary: Owns priority among care demands under scarcity.
nodes.excludes: Complete treatment planning after allocation.

nodes.name: Rural Emergency Triage Design
nodes.capability: Prioritize rural emergency patients safely under limited diagnostics, staffing, beds, and transfer access.
nodes.accepts: Presentations, vital signs, risk indicators, local capability, transfer conditions, and uncertainty.
nodes.produces: A simple acuity protocol with immediate actions, reassessment, and escalation paths.
nodes.boundary: Owns initial and continuing priority until definitive disposition.

nodes.boundary: Owns fit between need and available capability.

nodes.name: Equitable Priority

nodes.boundary: Owns distributive legitimacy of allocation.

nodes.boundary: Owns temporal validity of allocation.

nodes.excludes: Assuming averages describe every field.

nodes.name: Marginal Intervention Valuation
nodes.capability: Estimate incremental yield, cost, risk, and ecological value of management changes.
nodes.accepts: Candidate treatments, baselines, responses, prices, costs, and uncertainty.
nodes.produces: Comparable marginal value estimates for decisions.
nodes.boundary: Owns incremental rather than gross performance value.
nodes.excludes: Optimizing historical correlation without actionable contrast.

nodes.name: Public Information Trust System Design
nodes.capability: Design recurring public-information relationships that earn justified trust through warrant, openness, and accountability.
nodes.accepts: Information producers, audiences, claims, evidence, uncertainty, power, channels, and correction obligations.
nodes.produces: A trustworthy information service with inspectable warrant and responsive accountability.
nodes.boundary: Owns justified audience trust across publication and response.
nodes.excludes: Brand promotion, demands for unquestioning confidence, and disclosure without usability.

nodes.name: Reader Trust and Transparency Initiative
nodes.capability: Configure newsroom practices and reader interfaces that make journalistic warrant and accountability understandable.
nodes.accepts: Coverage, sources, editorial decisions, corrections, audiences, risks, workflows, and trust evidence.
nodes.produces: An inspectable reader-facing trust system integrated with newsroom work.
nodes.boundary: Owns transparency from reporting decisions through reader challenge and correction.
nodes.excludes: Publishing confidential sources, performative openness, and replacing verification with disclosure.

nodes.name: Editorial Decision Explainability
nodes.capability: Explain consequential editorial choices, limitations, and uncertainty at reader-appropriate depth.
nodes.accepts: Editorial decisions, evidence, uncertainty, constraints, and audience needs.
nodes.produces: Understandable explanations of how and why coverage took its form.
nodes.boundary: Owns explanation of editorial judgment.
nodes.excludes: Exposing protected deliberation or claiming neutrality eliminates judgment.

nodes.name: Reader Accountability Interface
nodes.capability: Enable readers to question, challenge, correct, and observe newsroom responses.
nodes.accepts: Reader concerns, published claims, evidence, response duties, and moderation constraints.
nodes.produces: A visible, fair challenge-and-response pathway.
nodes.boundary: Owns reciprocal accountability with readers.
nodes.excludes: Unmoderated abuse and popularity-based factual judgment.

nodes.name: Resilience-Oriented Distributed System Design
nodes.capability: Design distributed systems that preserve essential function and recover through diverse, bounded, adaptive capacities.
nodes.accepts: Services, nodes, state, dependencies, failures, loads, recovery objectives, and operating evidence.
nodes.produces: A fault-tolerant architecture with explicit degradation, recovery, and adaptation contracts.
nodes.boundary: Owns systemwide continuity under disturbance across distributed components.
nodes.excludes: Metaphorical biomimicry without technical guarantees and unlimited availability claims.

nodes.name: Functional Redundancy
nodes.capability: Provide independently failing alternatives capable of sustaining essential functions.
nodes.accepts: Critical functions, implementations, dependencies, capacities, and correlated failures.
nodes.produces: Diverse fallback capacity with explicit activation conditions.
nodes.boundary: Owns substitutability for essential function.
nodes.excludes: Duplicate components sharing the same failure mode.

nodes.name: Recovery Renewal
nodes.capability: Restore healthy capacity, state, and membership after disturbance without propagating latent damage.
nodes.accepts: Failed components, durable state, checkpoints, clean capacity, and recovery evidence.
nodes.produces: Verified regeneration of trustworthy service capacity.
nodes.boundary: Owns return from degraded operation to healthy function.
nodes.excludes: Failover without repair or unsafe automatic rejoining.

nodes.name: Living-System Stewardship
nodes.capability: Shape living-system relationships so valued functions persist, adapt, or recover under changing pressures.
nodes.accepts: Living communities, functions, disturbances, stressors, interventions, stakeholders, and uncertainty.
nodes.produces: A stewardship system sustaining functional ecological dynamics through time.
nodes.boundary: Owns deliberate management of interacting living processes.
nodes.excludes: Static preservation, isolated organism control, and purely mechanical systems.

nodes.name: Agroecological Pest Management
nodes.capability: Keep crop damage below acceptable thresholds through ecological regulation and non-synthetic interventions.
nodes.accepts: Crops, pests, beneficial organisms, fields, climate, practices, economics, and monitoring evidence.
nodes.produces: An adaptive pest-management strategy preserving production and ecological function.
nodes.boundary: Owns prevention, detection, suppression, and recovery across the crop system.
nodes.excludes: Routine synthetic pesticides, eradication promises, and calendar treatment without thresholds.

nodes.name: Pest Habitat Prevention
nodes.capability: Reduce conditions that enable damaging pest establishment, reproduction, persistence, and spread.
nodes.accepts: Pest life cycles, crop sequence, residue, habitat, planting, sanitation, and landscape context.
nodes.produces: A production environment less conducive to pest outbreaks.
nodes.boundary: Owns preventive manipulation of pest-supporting conditions.
nodes.excludes: Direct suppression after thresholds are exceeded.

nodes.name: Beneficial Regulation Capacity
nodes.capability: Build predator, parasitoid, competitor, and microbial capacity that regulates pests.
nodes.accepts: Pest ecology, beneficial organisms, habitat needs, field layout, and disturbance regimes.
nodes.produces: A functional biological-control community.
nodes.boundary: Owns ecological suppression through beneficial relationships.
nodes.excludes: Imported agents without ecological risk assessment.

nodes.name: Threshold-Governed Suppression
nodes.capability: Apply targeted non-synthetic controls when predicted damage justifies intervention.
nodes.accepts: Monitoring, action thresholds, crop stage, control options, costs, and non-target risks.
nodes.produces: Proportionate suppression decisions with bounded ecological effects.
nodes.boundary: Owns intervention after prevention and regulation prove insufficient.
nodes.excludes: Calendar spraying and action triggered by presence alone.

nodes.name: Rural Electric-Vehicle Charging Network
nodes.capability: Configure rural charging locations, capacity, power, access, and operations into a dependable statewide network.
nodes.accepts: Travel patterns, settlements, roads, vehicles, grid, sites, weather, users, economics, and growth uncertainty.
nodes.produces: A phased rural charging network providing reliable and equitable electric mobility.
nodes.boundary: Owns public and shared charging connectivity across a rural state.
nodes.excludes: Private home charging alone and uniform siting unrelated to travel needs.

nodes.name: Charging Reachability
nodes.capability: Place compatible charging so diverse trips remain feasible with tolerable detour and reserve.
nodes.accepts: Trip patterns, vehicle ranges, roads, destinations, seasons, and charger compatibility.
nodes.produces: A coverage topology with bounded travel gaps.
nodes.boundary: Owns geographic and functional reach of charging.
nodes.excludes: Site electrical feasibility and station economics.

nodes.name: Grid-Site Compatibility
nodes.capability: Fit charging capacity to site access, electrical supply, storage, generation, and upgrade feasibility.

nodes.name: Charging Service Continuity
nodes.capability: Keep charging usable through equipment, communications, weather, and power disruptions.
nodes.accepts: Stations, dependencies, failure modes, maintenance access, spares, and operating targets.

nodes.name: Embargo Incidence

nodes.name: Message Priority Semantics
nodes.capability: Define emergency message classes, authority, urgency, recipients, acknowledgment, and expiry.

nodes.boundary: Owns meaning and precedence of emergency communication.

nodes.boundary: Owns feedback conveyed by the inhabited environment.
nodes.excludes: Scoreboards, pervasive tracking, and prescribing optimal behavior.

nodes.excludes: Maze-like novelty and enforced social exposure.

bootstrap.summary: A first-principles bootstrap decomposes RootSolver into Problem Constitution, Explanatory Understanding, Resolution Synthesis, Resolution Commitment, Resolution Realization, and Resolution Regulation. Together they span the formation, direction, production, enactment, and correction of resolution without imposing a departmental workflow or domain taxonomy.

edges.role: Constitute the problem that resolution must address.
edges.rationale: Problem solving cannot be coherent without distinguishing the relevant present condition, valued outcome, and governing boundary.

edges.role: Represent the relevant starting situation.
edges.rationale: A discrepancy cannot be resolved without an account of what currently obtains.

edges.role: Define what counts as satisfactory improvement.
edges.rationale: Change is not resolution unless some outcomes are valued over others.

edges.role: Bound what the problem includes and permits.
edges.rationale: Without a boundary, relevance, responsibility, and admissible change remain indeterminate.

edges.role: Explain persistence, dependency, and leverage within the constituted problem.
edges.rationale: Effective intervention requires some warranted understanding of how actions can affect outcomes.

edges.role: Calibrate the informational basis of understanding.
edges.rationale: An explanation must distinguish supported claims from gaps and unreliable appearances.

edges.role: Model the relationships that produce and transmit change.
edges.rationale: Evidence becomes actionable only when organized into mechanisms or functional dependencies.

edges.role: Preserve material uncertainty in the explanatory account.
edges.rationale: Every finite model has unknowns whose effects must remain visible to later design and judgment.

edges.role: Create coherent possible resolutions.
edges.rationale: Understanding a problem does not by itself supply the interventions capable of changing it.

edges.role: Generate distinct change mechanisms.
edges.rationale: Resolution synthesis requires a possibility space rather than an unexamined default.

edges.role: Anticipate each candidate's broader effects.
edges.rationale: Candidates cannot be meaningfully developed without considering how their effects propagate.

edges.role: Integrate intervention elements into coherent candidates.
edges.rationale: Individually plausible actions may conflict unless configured as a mutually supporting resolution.

edges.role: Adopt a defensible course of resolution.
edges.rationale: Possibilities cannot guide action until tradeoffs, uncertainty, and ownership yield commitment.

edges.role: Judge candidates across valued outcomes.
edges.rationale: Commitment must distinguish alternatives using the problem's plural criteria.

edges.role: Test candidates against uncertainty and failure.
edges.rationale: A nominally preferred option may be unacceptable when its fragility is considered.

edges.role: Convert judgment into owned adoption.
edges.rationale: Assessment alone does not create the authority or willingness required for action.

edges.role: Produce the intended change in reality.
edges.rationale: A selected resolution remains hypothetical until agency and means realize its mechanism.

edges.role: Translate resolution intent into operable action.
edges.rationale: Conceptual decisions require a faithful bridge to concrete responsibilities and dependencies.

edges.role: Align the capabilities required for enactment.
edges.rationale: An executable configuration cannot operate without sufficient agency, resources, access, and coordination.

edges.role: Perform the intervention in the problem situation.
edges.rationale: Preparation and mobilization produce no resolution unless the change mechanism is actually exercised.

edges.role: Regulate resolution through feedback and learning.
edges.rationale: Problem solving occurs in changing, partly known conditions and therefore requires correction or justified closure.

edges.role: Acquire evidence about unfolding outcomes.
edges.rationale: Regulation requires observations independent of prior expectations.

edges.role: Locate what observed discrepancies mean.
edges.rationale: Feedback cannot guide correction until deviations are attributed to performance, understanding, criteria, or framing.

edges.role: Revise the affected problem-solving dimensions.
edges.rationale: Interpreted learning must alter the relevant resolution state or support deliberate closure.

bootstrap_topology.rationale: The bootstrap models Problem Solving as six mutually dependent outward capabilities: constituting what requires resolution, understanding how it behaves, synthesizing possible changes, committing under tradeoffs, realizing change, and regulating through feedback. Their children expose independent conceptual dimensions where another level materially improves routing. The carve is implementation-neutral and allows feedback to revise any earlier dimension.

cases.problem: Design a tax system for a developing nation
cases.framing: Shape a legitimate fiscal institution that jointly sustains public revenue, equitable burden sharing, economic participation, and feasible administration.

abstraction_ascent.why_more_general: Institutional Arrangement Design covers tax systems and other durable rule-and-authority structures.
abstraction_ascent.reframing_effect: Makes legitimacy, authority, enforcement, and induced behavior visible alongside revenue mechanics.

abstraction_ascent.why_more_general: System Shaping covers institutional arrangements as one class of deliberately configured interacting systems.
abstraction_ascent.reframing_effect: Requires attention to cross-component behavior, viability, and adaptation over time.

abstraction_ascent.why_more_general: RootSolver includes system shaping and fundamentally different modes of resolution.
abstraction_ascent.reframing_effect: Places structural design under the universal constitution, understanding, synthesis, commitment, realization, and regulation scaffold.

abstraction_ascent.why_more_general: RootSolver is the universal boundary for every resolvable problem.
abstraction_ascent.reframing_effect: Ensures the fiscal design is governed as a complete problem rather than treated as a tax formula.

topology_edges.role: Resolve problems by deliberately shaping an interacting system.
topology_edges.rationale: System shaping is a broad resolution mode contrasted with explaining, diagnosing, or expressing without structural intervention.

topology_edges.role: Shape systems whose operative structure consists of collectively binding rules and roles.
topology_edges.rationale: Institutional design reveals legitimacy, authority, incentives, and enforcement as dimensions not shared by every system.

topology_edges.role: Realize institutional design through a public revenue arrangement.
topology_edges.rationale: A tax system is a particular rule-governed institution with compulsory collection and fiscal incidence.

topology_edges.role: Secure sufficient and stable public revenue.
topology_edges.rationale: A tax system cannot fulfill its fiscal purpose without adequate yield.

topology_edges.role: Determine the effective allocation of burdens.
topology_edges.rationale: Incidence can vary independently of total yield and is necessary for legitimacy.

topology_edges.role: Make assessment, collection, and enforcement feasible.
topology_edges.rationale: An elegant statutory design fails if the state cannot operate it.

topology_edges.role: Manage participation, compliance, avoidance, and economic distortion.
topology_edges.rationale: Tax rules alter behavior, which affects every other dimension.

invocations.contribution: Govern the complete tax-system resolution.
Treat taxation as intervention in an adaptive social system.
Expose rules, authority, legitimacy, incentives, and enforcement.
Integrate the constitutive dimensions into one fiscal institution.
Estimate stable yields across growth, shocks, and compliance ranges.
Assess burdens by income, consumption, region, formality, and firm size.
Prefer observable bases and collection points compatible with limited capacity.
Limit evasion, informality traps, and penalties on productive participation.
Define the fiscal gap, development objectives, affected groups, and state-capacity boundary.
Model the economy, informality, compliance, incidence, and revenue leakage.
Construct alternative mixes of broad bases, progressive instruments, and simplified regimes.
Select a legitimate mix robust to uncertainty and political tradeoffs.
Phase legislation, registration, withholding, administration, and taxpayer support.
Track yield, incidence, compliance, distortion, and revise thresholds or enforcement.

cases.synthesis: A viable tax system emerges when sufficient revenue, fair effective incidence, administrable rules, and behaviorally credible incentives reinforce one another rather than optimizing one dimension in isolation.
cases.proposed_solution: Adopt a broad, low-rate consumption base with exemptions or targeted transfers for essentials; progressive personal income taxation concentrated on observable higher incomes; simple turnover-to-profit transition rules for small firms; and selective property, resource, and excise taxes. Phase implementation around withholding, digital invoicing, taxpayer IDs, independent appeals, and published incidence reviews, adjusting thresholds as administrative capacity and formal participation grow.

cases.framing: Reshape the care system surrounding heart-failure discharge so clinical stability, patient capability, continuity, and early feedback jointly prevent avoidable returns.

abstraction_ascent.why_more_general: Care Outcome Improvement covers this and other population-level care failures.
abstraction_ascent.reframing_effect: Moves attention from discharge instructions alone to the whole causal care configuration.

abstraction_ascent.why_more_general: Service System Shaping covers care improvement as one safety-critical service application.
abstraction_ascent.reframing_effect: Exposes journeys, handoffs, recipient participation, capacity, and feedback.

abstraction_ascent.why_more_general: System Shaping includes service systems and other interacting structures.
abstraction_ascent.reframing_effect: Frames readmission as emergent system behavior requiring coordinated structural change.

abstraction_ascent.why_more_general: RootSolver includes system shaping and non-shaping forms of resolution.
abstraction_ascent.reframing_effect: Subjects the intervention to the universal resolution scaffold.

abstraction_ascent.why_more_general: RootSolver is the universal problem-solving boundary.
abstraction_ascent.reframing_effect: Integrates framing, evidence, choice, enactment, and learning.

topology_edges.role: Shape systems that produce outcomes through recurring service interactions.
topology_edges.rationale: Service systems add journeys, encounters, handoffs, recipient participation, and capacity matching.

topology_edges.role: Shape care services around population health outcomes.
topology_edges.rationale: Care improvement adds clinical safety, patient vulnerability, and health-outcome obligations.

topology_edges.role: Improve a care outcome by preventing avoidable heart-failure readmissions.

batches.summary: The batch establishes System Shaping as the evidenced broad resolution mode, then differentiates institutional, service, software, provision, and organizational families. Later cases reuse and deepen those families through pricing, care allocation, reactive architecture, menu design, and talent development. Every case routes from RootSolver through its exact ascent and invokes all six universal problem-solving dimensions before producing a concrete proposal.

Batch 2 adds expressive and knowledge-forming root modes, extends system shaping across learning, experience, places, ecology, institutions, services, infrastructure, and regulation, and routes every case through the universal six-dimensional scaffold.

Batch 3 adds reusable families for developmental boundaries, assessment, building evolution, functional music, and twenty concrete composites, all routed through evidenced broad modes and decomposed into constitutive dimensions.
Batch 4 adds twenty problem-specific composites and reusable intermediate families, routing each through adjacent abstractions, all six universal dimensions, and constitutive subject decompositions.

Twenty problems were routed root-first through evidenced resolution modes, reusable families, and subject-specific composites, then decomposed into governing conceptual dimensions and concise proposals.

Batch 6 adds ten specific composites and reusable families for developmental routines, incentive governance, embedded analytics, public trust, resilience, living stewardship, rural charging, simulation, emergency communication, and learning-engagement buildings.
